name: Optical current sensor
summary: Current sensor using light in an optical fibre around the conductor, whose polarisation changes with the magnetic field.
description: An optical current sensor measures current from the rotation of polarised light in a fibre wound around the conductor, a magneto-optic effect proportional to the enclosed magnetic field. It is used in HV and DC applications where conventional CTs are bulky or where saturation and insulation are concerns.

The sensor head connects through fibre to an electronics unit, which usually outputs digital sampled values to protection and metering devices. The symbol does not show the electronics unit, its supply or the data interface, all of which must be drawn for the measurement chain to be complete.
readingNotes: Find the electronics unit that converts the optical signal.
Check the data interface to protection devices.
distinction: An optical current sensor uses light in fibre; a conventional CT uses magnetic induction in a winding.
